title: CmdPal: Applications are launched with an outdated PATH

judgment.rationale: The original report describes an outdated PATH after a change. A second reporter supplied a controlled transcript on 0.102.3101 showing a general user environment variable remaining stale in CmdPal-launched Zed, while Start and a PowerToys restart pick up the change. The precise shell-launch propagation and safe refresh strategy remain to be tested.
evidence: The 0.102.3101 transcript compares the same variable before and after the Windows environment settings change and tests both elevated and non-elevated PowerToys: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/42306#issuecomment-6960037591.

A contributor recently said they had investigated but not implemented a fix, and described WM_SETTINGCHANGE and Explorer-mediated launch as alternatives: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/42306#issuecomment-6961010605.

The current All Apps desktop launch uses Process.Start with UseShellExecute=true, while packaged apps use a separate activation path: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/00d85a4c73c2ec33da7a9c25d1a3581b3d4c4359/src/modules/cmdpal/ext/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.Apps/AppCommand.cs.

The discussion notes the shell execution path may affect propagation and points to PowerToys Run's environment-refresh precedent: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/42306#issuecomment-6962356772.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the controlled environment change and test the actual All Apps shell-launch behavior before choosing a refresh mechanism.

fix_assessment.rationale: No covering implementation was found in linked or fork-side work. The contributor identified alternatives but explicitly had not implemented them; coordination with that contributor is appropriate.

proposed_fixes.title: Refresh the environment used for newly launched desktop apps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A long-lived CmdPal launch path may propagate its startup environment after Windows user or machine variables change; shell delegation still needs confirmation.
plan: Trace the All Apps desktop launch and verify whether its shell execution uses CmdPal's environment after a settings-change notification.
Choose an environment refresh or shell-mediated launch approach based on that result, preserving process-specific values, user and machine PATH merging, expansion, and deletions.
Add regression coverage for changes after startup and check packaged activation separately rather than assuming it follows the same path.
verification: Change a test user variable and PATH after CmdPal starts, launch a fully closed desktop app, and verify it receives the updated values without restarting PowerToys.
Test deleted variables, user and machine PATH, protected process-specific values, and elevated and non-elevated launch behavior.

confidence.rationale: The controlled report and launch source support a stale environment, but the shell propagation and refresh approach have not been tested.

issue_context.summary: Applications launched from CmdPal retain stale environment values after Windows environment settings change.
known_information: The original 0.94.2 report says an added PATH entry is unavailable in VS Code launched through CmdPal until PowerToys restarts.
A 0.102.3101 comparison shows a user variable remains at its old value in CmdPal-launched Zed while Start and restarting PowerToys use the new value.
The contributor who suggested a fix said the two candidate approaches had not been implemented.
inferences: The long-lived launch path may carry stale process environment to a new desktop app, but UseShellExecute can delegate to the shell and must be checked.
issue_context.analysis: The newer transcript shows the issue is not limited to PATH or elevation. PowerToys Run has a refresh helper, but copying its approach without testing shell propagation and protected overrides would be premature.
initial_investigation: The current All Apps desktop AppCommand uses Process.Start with UseShellExecute=true; packaged activation uses IApplicationActivationManager.
PowerToys Run's EnvironmentHelper merges user and machine variables and handles protected values, deletion and expansion.
Issue https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/46577 was closed as a duplicate; no linked upstream or fork implementation was found.

actions.label: Approve Refresh the environment used for CmdPal-launched processes

reproduce.title: Compare CmdPal and Start environment after a user-variable change
prerequisites: A desktop app with a shell or environment viewer that can be fully exited between launches.
A test executable available only through the new user PATH directory.
setup: Create a harmless user variable CMDPAL_ENV_PROBE=before in Windows environment settings, then fully exit and restart PowerToys and the test app.
steps: Launch the app from CmdPal and confirm CMDPAL_ENV_PROBE is before; exit the app fully.
Change the variable to after in Windows environment settings, then launch the app from CmdPal and inspect the process value.
Exit it fully, launch it from Start, and compare; restart PowerToys and repeat the CmdPal launch. Remove the test variable afterward.
Add a harmless directory to the user PATH while PowerToys remains running; launch VS Code (or the reported app) from CmdPal and from Start, then compare the child-process PATH.
From both child processes, run the test executable by name and compare command resolution.
Restart PowerToys and repeat the CmdPal launch to distinguish stale inherited state from launch-time propagation.
reproduce.expected_result: A newly launched app receives the updated user variable without restarting PowerToys, matching Start. Both launches also resolve the test executable by name.
